title: Which Appliances Use the Most Electricity in a Home?

seo.title: Which Appliances Use the Most Electricity in a Home?

content_html:
The biggest household electricity users are usually equipment that makes heat or removes heat for long periods: electric heating and cooling, water heating, clothes drying, cooking, and in some homes pumps or electric-vehicle charging. Nameplate power matters, but operating hours matter just as much.

Start with electric heating, cooling, and water heating

A heat pump, central air conditioner, electric resistance heater, or water heater can run for many hours and account for a large share of monthly use. Climate, insulation, and thermostat settings make results vary widely between homes.

Dryers and ovens draw high power for shorter periods

An electric dryer or oven may draw several kilowatts while running, but monthly energy depends on how many loads or meals you run. Do not rank appliances by instantaneous wattage alone.

Smaller loads can add up when they run continuously

A dehumidifier, pool pump, aquarium, home server, or older refrigerator may draw less power per hour but operate for much of the day. Long runtime can turn a moderate load into a meaningful monthly cost.

Use your bill or metering to identify your own largest loads

Compare monthly bills, utility usage history, and appropriate plug-in energy meters for cord-connected appliances. General rankings help prioritize, but your own data shows where efficiency changes will matter most.

faq.answer: An electric dryer or oven may draw several kilowatts while running, but monthly energy depends on how many loads or meals you run. Do not rank appliances by instantaneous wattage alone.

faq.question: How can I find the biggest electricity users in my own home?
